title: coordkit event envelope v2
description: One append-only JSON event per line in the coordination log. v1 events (no schema_version) are read tolerantly as 1.0: readers pass them through VERBATIM and treat any absent v2 field as its default — no on-read rewrite happens. (schema/migrations/0001_v1_to_v2.sh is an OPTIONAL offline/manual up-converter and is NOT invoked on the read path.) Stored lines are NEVER rewritten.

schema_version.description: Envelope version, major.minor. Readers MUST ignore unknown fields and treat a missing value as "1.0".

eid.description: Content-addressed id over canonical(event minus eid,sig). The cross-replica DEDUP key and audit anchor. e.g. "sha256:9f3c…" (blake3 if b3sum is present).

id.description: Sortable unique id (ULID-like). Tiebreak + display only; not the dedup key.

actor.description: STABLE per (machine + user + clone) site id. Partitions the committed filespace so two writers never touch the same segment file.

clock.description: Per-actor clock: wall-ms + counter. AS IMPLEMENTED the cross-instance total order is sort by (clock.p, clock.c, actor), and it IS the transport and shared-ledger read path: transports/lib.sh __total_order backs union reads, ledger projections use ordered stream position, and shared-session incremental reads persist max clock.c per actor so late-before-global-watermark arrivals remain visible. No cross-replica decision is based on replica-local `seq`. LIMITATION: because `clock.p` is unsynchronised per-machine wall-clock ms and `clock.c` is not reconciled against peers, ordering ACROSS actors is effectively wall-clock last-writer-wins and is subject to inter-machine clock skew (`clock.c`/`actor` only break exact-millisecond ties). Within one actor the counter and resulting cursor are monotonic.

c.description: AS IMPLEMENTED: a plain local monotonic counter, incremented once per emitted event and persisted per-actor in ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}/clock.state. It is NOT reconciled against other actors — nothing observes peers' clocks or advances past a max observed value. True cross-replica clock advancement (Lamport-style) is RESERVED for future work and NOT YET IMPLEMENTED.

seq.description: LOCAL-only convenience counter (per physical log). NOT authoritative for cross-machine order — use clock.

host.description: Producer host adapter identity. Derived from adapter/runtime signals and independent of any user-facing app name.

user.description: Advisory producer metadata stamped locally from $USER. Relay bearer grants authenticate access to a room, but the server deliberately preserves the content-addressed event unchanged and therefore does not rewrite this field. Do not use event.user for authorization.

type.description: Event type. KNOWN types: note, decision, question, answer, task, claim, done, block. This list is DOCUMENTATION, not a closed set — readers MUST tolerate unknown types as opaque notes, so validation accepts any string. Producers SHOULD stick to the known types.

subject.description: Reconciliation key: the latest non-superseded event per subject wins.

body.description: Free-text payload. A task body may carry 'dep:<subject>' tokens for ordering.

refs.description: Content refs (eids) instead of fragile numeric seq refs.

lease.description: ALWAYS an object from v2 onward (never a bare scalar). null when not a claim.

until.description: epoch seconds the lease is valid until

supersedes.description: RESERVED — eid of the prior version of this subject, an explicit version chain for audit/history. NOT YET IMPLEMENTED: the emitter always writes null and no reader consults it; subject reconciliation is done positionally (latest event per subject wins), not by walking this chain.

sig.description: RESERVED — detached ed25519 signature over canonical(event minus sig). NOT YET IMPLEMENTED: nothing signs and nothing verifies; the emitter always writes null. The field is carved out now so signed events stay eid-compatible later (eid is computed over the event minus eid and sig, so adding a signature never changes an event's id).
